body: BINDING ON YOUR CURRENT AMENDMENT - read before finishing Laws.scala. The three PopulationLaws match on the error case so the refusal is proved to be the RIGHT refusal, not an incidental failure. Your candidate splits view mismatch from recall mismatch. Two migrations look identical in a diff: WIDEN the match to accept either new case - green, quick, and the law is now STRICTLY WEAKER, because a bug returning the RECALL error for a VIEW mismatch would sail through and nothing would notice; or SPLIT it so each law matches ITS OWN case, making the law STRONGER than before, since the old FingerprintMismatch could not distinguish those failures at all. THE SPLIT IS REQUIRED. A migration prompted by a type getting more precise must leave the law more precise, or the precision was purchased and thrown away. If you find a path that can legitimately produce either error, do NOT widen - post it and I will rule, because that would mean the errors are less separable than the candidate claims. Credit where due: this is m1's observation, and m1 WROTE those three laws under bd-01M158KA75HGGM118P3SQ1RHYK - it has offered to be asked rather than reverse-engineered, so take that offer if anything is non-mechanical. Laws.scala stays yours; m1 is consulting, not claiming. Your refusal proof was exactly the required order and isolating it by running only PopulationSuite without compiling laws was the right touch.
